key_insight: Biased-noise qubits can dramatically reduce fault-tolerance overhead only when the hardware operations preserve the noise bias, especially through a CX gate or equivalent measurement-based substitute.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware design, the paper shows that the right gate set and readout primitives can turn strongly biased physical noise into a practical advantage for lower-overhead error correction and magic-state preparation.
method: Classify fault-tolerant protocols by the available bias-preserving operations.
Compare CZ-only architectures against architectures with a bias-preserving CX gate.
Extend the CX-based advantages to measurement-based schemes using high-fidelity QND multi-qubit Z readout.
evidence_signal: The review argues, based on error-rate analysis and overhead comparisons, that CZ-only syndrome extraction can erase the benefit of noise bias at experimentally relevant error rates, while CX-enabled designs can recover substantial gains.
watch_item: The main limitation is that the most powerful overhead reductions depend on hardware support for bias-preserving CX or high-fidelity multi-qubit Z readout, which may be difficult to realize in many platforms.
paper_title: Biased-noise qubits: a guide to efficient fault-tolerance using the hierarchy of errors
